group_on8192.phase_instruction:
Group the supplied Git changes by distinct change purposes.

Group changes that implement, test, or consume the same
behavioral change or shared contract.

Do not create separate purposes for different parts of
the same behavioral change.

Separate changes only when they represent independent
behavioral goals. Sharing a file, package, import, or helper
is not sufficient evidence of a shared purpose.

Base each grouping decision only on concrete changes
supported by the input. Do not infer unseen requirements
or behavior.

Assign every supplied file ID exactly once to one permitted group label. Equal labels mean the same commit group.
If a file contains multiple change-purpose candidates, treat them
as one purpose only when all are inseparable parts of one concrete
behavioral or contract change. Otherwise assign that file a group
label used by no other file, even if other files implement or test
one of its purposes. Partial dependencies or a connected dependency
graph alone do not justify merging. Never split or duplicate a file.

For the Category phase, classify each finalized group from its own current Git diff.
Use docs for documentation-only changes, including new sections or explanations of existing commands.
Use feat for new observable program behavior. Use fix for corrections to erroneous program behavior. Tests accompanying an implementation inherit that implementation's purpose. Use test for test-only changes.
Use refactor for restructuring without observable change. Use perf only with performance purpose and evidence. Other allowed types retain their Conventional Commits meaning.
For breaking_evidence_ref, inspect whether the diff shows a supported public API, CLI, configuration or stored-format incompatibility. An internal implementation change or new internal field alone does not establish a public incompatibility. Choose none when no supported public incompatibility is visible. Choose unresolved only when a specific public incompatibility is suspected but lacks available evidence. Otherwise choose an applicable observed evidence reference.
